# Fixed-defect Schur recovery from explicit subgroup-orbit frames

28 October2026. **Author theorem candidate; independent review pending.** This extends the preserved rectangular construction to unequal and nonrectangular local sectors. It is not a full decoder for arbitrary positive-entropy mixed sources. No unknown environment, Clebsch–Gordan basis or exponentially large Choi matrix is accessed.

## 1. Objective and supplied input

Let lambda,mu be partitions of k, with real Young-orthogonal Specht spaces V_lambda,V_mu of dimensions d,D. Fix an integer defect j, 0<=j<k. Let H=S_(k−j) fix the last j labels pointwise and L=[S_k:H]=(k)_j. Let S be any selected set of partitions nu with nu_1>=k−j. A rank ceiling, dimension cutoff or other computable predicate may further restrict S.

The target is the full Choi error space consisting of ALL multiplicity copies of these nu in Hom(V_lambda,V_mu). The corresponding orthogonal isotropic reference channel and the physical positive error weights are those of the universal Schur code. Its decoder input also includes an actual code-isometry circuit C:C^K→V_lambda and its inverse, not an exponential dense table. K>=2 and d>=2 are the substantive case; K1 is a trivial one-dimensional output. Random-code averaging assumes code choices independent of physical weights; any approximate-design moment error remains paid.

Central primary source: Rizzo et al., *Universal quantum coding*, arXiv2609.38038v1, equations14,63–66,74–79,146–152 and implementation discussion after175. That source defines the reference/error-weight interface and leaves efficient polar implementation open. The present contribution is an explicit access construction for fixed defect, not a new statement that QSVT implements a supplied matrix. Standard Schur branching, subgroup averaging and QSVT are credited ingredients. Astra's separately reviewed gap-free error-frame recovery lemma supplies the total decoder once access is built.

## 2. Explicit H-invariant matrix units

Restrict the Young bases to their first k−j entries. A tableau of shape lambda is uniquely a prefix tableau T of some shape alpha⊢k−j and a suffix branching path q of length j ending at lambda. Similarly use p for mu. For each common alpha and every pair(p,q), define a partial isometry

    E_(alpha,p,q)|T,q> = |T,p>,

zero on other suffix paths. This is an explicit map V_lambda→V_mu

The existence of H-invariant seeds(s>0) does not imply that a particular selected set S has nonzero image. For example, lambda differs from mu and S contains only the trivial irrep. Therefore the reference-channel and beta formulas in Section7 apply only when N=rank(Pi_S)>0. If N=0, W_A=0, the selected physical good mass is zero, and the total decoder outputs its fixed fallback. No negative beta formula is used. The algorithm need not solve a hidden-rank problem to detect this case: its zero contraction already implements fallback. The s=0 early branch remains directly detectable from enumerated paths.

The source-weight guarantee is on the physically selected error space, never arbitrary redundant M-dimensional weights. Random-code mean statements require the physical weights to be independent of the code. The bound in Section8 assumes0<=c/k<=1 (otherwise use the trivial probability bound1), and a maximal eigenvalue at least1−c/k; it is not a finite-data certificate for that promise.

# Conventional reblocking removes the claimed dilute asymptotic opening

28 October 2026. Load-bearing comparison correction identified by the parent researcher after the inner corollary was received. The inner theorem remains valid at its actual scope. The dilute-family asymptotic consequence must **not** be presented as a newly enabled recovery capability on the strength of that theorem alone.

## Equally informed alternative

For the same unknown iid source family delta_n<=c/n^z, 0<z<1, choose smaller blocks h=floor(n^(z/2)). No environment reconstruction is required. The block trace distance from the unknown dominant pure tensor power is exactly

    1−(1−delta_n)^h <= h delta_n <= c n^(−z/2).

Apply ordinary universal unknown-pure-state Schur entanglement concentration to each block, with the same fixed entropy margin H(psi_B)>=R+Delta. A fixed-dimensional total version outputs floor(hR) ebits with pure-source failure tending to zero (Schur concentration and the entropy margin supply the dimension tail). Contractivity of trace distance adds at most c n^(−z/2) to the block infidelity. Thus, for any fixed epsilon_0>0, all sufficiently large n give block infidelity below epsilon_0 without the mixed reference polar decoder.

The same independent-block q-ary outer CSS/GRS premise can now be used on B'=floor(n/h) blocks. Its alphabet q'=2^floor(hR) eventually exceeds B'. The asymptotic output rate is again at least (1−4gamma)R, with error exp[−Omega(B')]=exp[−Omega(n^(1−z/2))] at fixed gamma>epsilon_0. Its circuit/source independence assumptions are exactly those used in the proposed low-defect composition. This alternative uses smaller blocks and avoids the large k^{O(j)} orbit tables; no resource advantage for the low-defect protocol has been established.

An alternative constant rescaling h=floor(theta n^z), theta sufficiently small relative to epsilon_0/c, also reduces pure-approximation block error below the desired constant while preserving the asymptotic concentration rate. Therefore even insisting on the exponent z rather than z/2 does not rescue a distinct asymptotic capability.
